column1: # One line per assertion that is NOT expected to pass. A key that is absent from this file
# is expected to PASS; there are no PASS rows. Columns are tab-separated:
# VACUOUS_EXPECTED_FAILURE is an `expect failure` row that gie would score a pass but which
# measured nothing: the operation could not be created for a reason unrelated to what the row
# asserts. It is neither a pass nor a failure, and it is excluded from both sides of the
# Regenerate (never hand-sort; the writer emits the canonical order):
# Hand-written reasons are preserved across regeneration for entries whose outcome is
# unchanged, so it is worth explaining WHY, not just THAT, an assertion fails.

column3: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE -- an upstream defect, which this expectation encodes. PROJ's krovak inverse is not the inverse of PROJ's own forward: krovak_setup assigns P->a, P->es and P->e (9.8.1:src/projections/krovak.cpp:287-289) but never P->ra, and never calls pj_calc_ellipsoid_params, so under PJ_IO_UNITS_CLASSIC the forward scales by P->a = Bessel's 6377397.155 (9.8.1:src/fwd.cpp:142-143) while the inverse scales by P->ra = 1/6378137 left over from +ellps=GRS80 (9.8.1:src/inv.cpp:92-93). PROJ's own round trip misses by 138.6 m at the Guidance Note 7-2 point. proj4j derives totalScale from Bessel in both directions and round-trips exactly, and PROJ asked for the same inverse with +ellps=bessel reproduces proj4j's value exactly. Decision: keep proj4j's behaviour and change no code; matching PROJ would mean writing the stale reciprocal in on purpose. See KrovakProjection's class javadoc. Inverse of (200, 100) m: proj4j 24.836219260 59.758404029 vs expected 24.836218919 59.758403933, deviation 21.942407 mm, tolerance 0.100000 mm, metric GEODESIC_FROM_RADIANS.

GRID DELIBERATELY NOT VENDORED. require_grid names us_nga_egm08_25.tif, the EGM2008 geoid at 2.5', which is 80,585,622 bytes. GitHub warns above 50 MB per file and a vendored copy can never be taken back out of the history, so this row is left skipped on purpose rather than for want of a licence or an implementation: the file is NGA public domain and PROJ marks it direct_download=1, open_license=1. The sibling French block (#1:0) was the same shape and closed in 2.3.0 by vendoring fr_ign_RAF20.tif, 342,920 bytes. If ever wanted, this closes by copying the grid into proj-data-cdn/ and adding a row to NOTICE-gie.md section 4 -- nothing else.

GRID VENDORED, CRS TYPE NOT BUILDABLE. This row was a SKIP until 2.3.0, when fr_ign_RAF20.tif (342,920 bytes, Etalab Open Licence, NOTICE-gie.md section 4) was vendored under proj-data-cdn/ and GieGridAvailability.OnClasspath was taught to search that directory as well as proj-data/. The grid resolves; the block now runs and fails for a reason that was hidden behind the missing file. crs_src is EPSG:9785, RGF93 v2b + NGF-IGN69 height, a COMPOUND CRS, and DatabaseCrsFactory builds only geodetic types -- so this needs compound CRS construction from the database, vertical CRS construction, and an operation selector that can pair a compound source with a 3D geographic target through a geoid grid. That is its own release, the same family of work as projected CRSs from the database. The ratio is unaffected either way: SKIP and FAIL both sit in the denominator and neither is a pass. Note the content hash moved from 66d05acf to b3dab9b5 and the corpus index moved with it -- no corpus text changed. A skipped block is recorded against its require_grid line and a running one against its expect line, and the hash covers the assertion text, so the key follows the outcome here.

OPERATION NOT FOUND, NOT ARITHMETIC WRONG. Both CRSs resolve and an operation is built, but it applies no shift at all: the output is the input, digit for digit, so the answer lands 344.35 mm away at epoch 2026.0. The arithmetic is already correct -- fed PROJ's own pipeline for this pair (projinfo -s EPSG:7843 -t EPSG:7912 -o PROJ), proj4j's engine returns -33.862297057 151.207701181 -0.001013 against gie's -33.862297056 151.207701181 -0.00101, about 0.09 mm, well inside the 0.1 mm tolerance. What is missing is discovery. EPSG:8049, the time-dependent 15-parameter Helmert this needs, is published between the GEOCENTRIC pair EPSG:7789 and EPSG:7842, and the selector does not compose geographic->geocentric->operation->geocentric->geographic: measured against this tree, db.operationsBetween("EPSG","7843","EPSG","7912") returns 0 while ("EPSG","7789","EPSG","7842") returns 1. That is a selector change and it is out of scope for 2.3.0. Block 3 above uses the same CRS pair and passes, but only by luck: EPSG:8049's static terms are all zero and only its rotation RATES are non-zero, so at block 3's epoch of 2020.0 -- which is the operation's own t_epoch -- "no shift" happens to be the right answer. Block 4 is the same request six years later, where the rates have accumulated, and there "no shift" is simply wrong. Measured: deviation 344.350595 mm, tolerance 0.100000 mm, metric GEODESIC_FROM_DEGREES; got -33.862300000 151.207700000 0.000000000 2026.000000000
